$note: A REWRITE pivot: this model's candidates for one variable across the cells it wrote, each beside the original and its gate result. Truth is Reading/Database/templates/by_variable (generated from by_axis).

variants.candidate: You want things far more easily than you claim them. Put one goal in writing with a date beside it. Move a fixed sum into savings on the same day each month. Tell the person you love one plan for the year and keep to it. Finish the small thing before you start another.
variants.original: Ownership is ambition slowed down enough to keep. Automate a monthly amount into one long-term asset and stop renegotiating it. Review what you hold twice a year. Add slowly, and only what you intend to keep for a decade.

variants.candidate: Holding yourself up takes more than you are taking in. Sleep a full night before a big decision rather than after it. Share one weekly meal with a peer who is not competing with you. Let someone carry one thing for you each month. Sit down for ten minutes before you say yes.
variants.original: Vitality is grown, never summoned. Get daylight before noon, move every day even briefly, keep green things and green places near you. Protect one truly free evening a week. Start one small thing and let finishing it feed the next.

variants.candidate: You reach for the answer while the lesson is still landing. Ahead of a decision, read a full chapter instead of the summary. Ask one person who knows more than you and wait for the whole reply. Keep a notebook by the bed for the thought that arrives late. Sleep on anything that can wait a night.
variants.original: Understanding arrives on its own schedule and only through an open door. Hold one screen-free hour before bed. Take the walk before the decision. Keep a note of what surfaces there, because it will be the truest thinking you do.

variants.candidate: You hold your work in until it is perfect, and perfect never comes. Let the rough version out. Play the half-written song for one friend. Post the drawing with the mistake left in. Tell a child the story before you know its ending. Say one unchecked opinion out loud.
variants.original: Light is part of how work finishes. Show one finished thing a week, publicly and on purpose. Say yes to the toast, the talk, the intro. When something stalls, share it half-done and let being seen restart it.

variants.candidate: Nothing of yours gets finished until something outside you says when. Give one deadline a month to someone else to hold. Take charge of the next small emergency at home without being asked. Send the work with one mistake left in it. Write one rule on a card and keep it for a week.
variants.original: Growth loves resistance it respects. Put your work in front of one demanding person on a schedule, monthly at least. Ask for the harshest note first. Treat every review on the calendar as training, never as threat.
